content.title: About
content.content: Kidney beans are large, kidney‑shaped legumes known for their deep red color. In canned form they are fully cooked and ready to eat, and the reduced‑sodium version (2151 mg/100 g) makes them suitable for low‑salt diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the bean’s shape, which resembles a human kidney.
Red beans contain anthocyanins that give them their vivid color.
Canning preserves most of the bean’s nutrients, including protein and fiber.
They are a staple in Mexican, Creole, and South American cuisines.
Reduced‑sodium cans achieve lower salt levels by substituting part of the salt with flavorful spices.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: A typical serving (about 130 g) provides roughly 8 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps keep you feeling full.

items.title: Contains iron and folate
items.content: These micronutrients are essential for blood formation and preventing anemia.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Reduced salt makes this product a good choice for people monitoring blood pressure.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in kidney beans help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Raw toxicity
items.content: Uncooked kidney beans contain phytohaemagglutinin, a toxic protein. Canning destroys it, but raw beans must never be eaten.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Legumes can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals; introduce them gradually.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some people may experience an allergic reaction to beans.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While nutritious, beans are relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned kidney beans can be tossed into salads, soups, chili, stews, and pasta dishes. They are ready to use straight from the can—simply drain the liquid, optionally rinse, and add. For a milder flavor, rinse briefly with cold water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 3–4 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
